summary:
I reviewed the merged build at 72a1066 in first person, using side view only to check mechanics. I recorded 61 probe and bot acts with Movie Maker, one Godot process at a time. The probe r3_probe.gd (built from gap_probe and ko_probe) measures each rendered frame after the camera has moved: nearest own and other mesh to the lens, share of the view, and lens to world boxes.

What holds:
- **Launches into walls.** Bodies crumple at the end wall and the building front (deepest non-brim vertex 0.098 m for 5 ticks). The lens stays clear: 0.275 m or more, at most 47% of the view.
- **Uppercut from behind.** The body pitches away from the lens (0.399 m, 37%).
- **Point-blank throw into a wall.** 0.256 m.
- **Comeback.** A simultaneous KO of three dummies comes back together; a dummy beside an occupied post comes back 0.8 m ahead and waits 300 ticks without walking.
- **Finisher flashes after hit-04.** Each shows on exactly the 2 frames after the ink frame for the shove, backfist, stomp kick, push kick and pipe smash.
- **Warm-up.** Only pixel (0,0) of frame 0 is inked.
- **Damage looks.** 290 of 308 frames are bit-identical to the pre-perf-02 baseline, the rest at 67.6 dB or better.
- **Ragdoll acts.** All 13 first-person ragdoll_bot acts match the gap reviewer's rag_all, apart from the intended changes (the folded far arm, the from-behind pitch).
- **KO view in the plain cases.** Standing, holding, facing a wall, from behind, a heavy launch, near the curb, near a crate, and F2 mid-KO all read as a short out-of-body moment.

What fails:
1. The KO view's return goes wherever the mouse points. With the look turned 120 degrees while down, the lens dives through the player's own face and chest: own body 50-75% of the view for 11 frames, then a 66% pop. Even without a turn, the own cap and face sweep across 25-35% of the view on the way back.
2. In a corner the KO view sits 0.13 m inside the building front, and the own shirt fills 52-68% of the view for the whole KO. With dummies on both sides it hovers 0.32 m over a dummy's head and the body is clipped at the edge of the view.
3. Smaller items:
   - The hook's re-posed far fist comes 0.200 m from the lens on open floor and 0.145 m against a building front.
   - A comeback dead ahead at 0.8 m fills 56% of the view.
   - The first-person haymaker's delayed flash can't be seen (0.06-0.2% of the screen).

I edited no tracked files; git status is clean apart from captures/.

open_question_notes:
**KO view as a player (defaults 1.7 m out, 1.6 m up, 40 degrees down; 0.8 s out, 0.5 s back).**
- It reads as a short out-of-body moment.
  - KO1 timing: the lens starts leaving when the blow's hitstop ends (movie m67) and is fully out at m112. The body lands at m84. It holds through the KO and starts back at the revive (m234). It is in the eyes at m263, one frame before FREE.
  - About 3.3 s out of the body in all.
  - The body fills about half the view's width but only 8% of the grid cells. The attacker is cut at the hips by the top edge, so you can't see who KO'd you (ko1_all.png). The distance looks right to me.
  - The first 0.25 s of the leave (m67-82) shows floor and falling legs.
- The return is the weak part (finding 1).

**Non-KO knockdown (KD1, kd1_all.png).**
- The navy belly slab covers up to 74% of the view.
- Over 50% covered for 63 frames, own mesh 0.059 m from the lens.
- About 1.3 s in all, from the hit to free.

**HUD during the KO view.**
- The HP bar stays: empty while KO'd, yellow again at the revive. The centre dot stays over the body (ko1_all.png).

**Wall reaction (default: stop and drop).**
- End wall uppercut: the body crumples down the wall, with blood on it (walls_fp.png row 1).
- Building-front haymaker: same, the splats stay on the wall (row 5).
- Curb uppercut: still a stiff Y-armed rise and straight drop in front of the curb (row 2).

**Part-body choice of the push (stale cache).** Nothing visible changed against the gap reviewer's rag_all.

**Flash size and flurry strobe (hit-01, grab-05), numbers after hit-04.**
- Method: share of the 1600x900 screen that the flash changes by more than 20 luma. Flash on against --tune=hit_flash_strength=0, effects RNG seeded (fin_probe), so only flash pixels differ.

| Hit | Frames | Share of screen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jab | 29-30 | 8.0% |
| Each flurry body blow (7 at 8.6 Hz) | | 24-25% |
| Finisher shove (impact frame 123-124) | 125-126 | 7.9 / 9.4% |
| Spinning backfist | 300-301 | 6.1 / 7.1% |
| Stomp kick | 640-641 | 2.5 / 3.1% |
| Push kick | 782-783 | 2.2 / 3.1% |
| Pipe smash | 1287-1288 | 6.5 / 8.3% |
| First-person haymaker | 940-941 | 0.06 / 0.20% (finding 5) |

- Every flash lasts exactly 2 frames, and nothing else differs.

**Combat log over the knee (grab-03).** Not re-checked.

**Movie size.** Movies come out 1600x900 even with --resolution 1280x720 (fin.log, 'recording movie in 1600×900'), as the ragdoll reviewer noted.

findings.title: KO view: the return into the eyes follows the mouse look and keeps the head layer drawn, so it dives through the player's own face and chest (up to 75% of the view, then a 66% pop)
findings.detail:
**How the return works.** It blends the KO pose back into `live`, the eye view from _follow(). That view uses player.get_look_basis(), which mouse look keeps changing while the player lies KO'd (player.gd _process() does not check the state). The body only turns to the look on the tick it is FREE again (_tick_control() sets rotation.y = look_yaw only when _can_steer_body()). Meanwhile the head layer (head, neck, chest, shoulders) is re-hidden only once the weight reaches exactly 0 (first_person_camera.gd:294).

**What the player sees.** Suppose Game-boy moves the mouse during the 2.5 s KO, which is likely since the view gives him nothing else to do. The lens then returns to a look that doesn't match the body getting up. It flies through his own face, neck and chest box with all of them drawn, then pops clear when the layer hides.

**Without a turn.** The path still sweeps the own cap and face across the left of the view at 0.6-0.9 m. Then the lens passes within 0.25 m of drawn head-layer meshes for 11 frames, 0.000 m at the closest (it ends up inside them, so they are back-face culled). The lead saw this as 'the own head large for a frame or two'.

**Untested.** tests/test_ko_view.gd never turns the look while the player is down.
findings.repro:
godot --path . --write-movie captures/review_r3look/ko3.avi --fixed-fps 60 --resolution 1280x720 res://captures/review_r3look/r3_probe.tscn -- --act=KO13 (or KO14, or KO1 for the plain return).

KO13: player at 3 HP, a sparring jab KOs him. 40 ticks into the KO, look_yaw turns 120 degrees over 60 ticks, as a mouse would. Then the revive and the return.

In play: get KO'd by the sparring dummy and move the mouse sideways while lying.
findings.suggested_fix:
Presentation first:
1. In _ko_view_mix(), while easing back in, hide VIS_FP_HIDDEN again as soon as _head_clear_of(lens) turns false: the mirror of the lift, with the layer still out of view at that point. Or fade the KO pose's look so the head leaves the frame before the lens reaches it.
2. Build the return's target from the body's facing, not the free look. Either:
   - have PlayerCharacter ignore mouse yaw and pitch while KO'd and getting up (or set look_yaw to rotation.y at _revive());
   - or let the camera ease the look toward the rig's facing during the return.
   Either way the lens comes back to the eyes the body actually has, and the body doesn't snap at FREE.
3. Add test_ko_view cases with the look turned ±45 and 120 degrees while down: own body at most a third of the view, nothing within 0.25 m, no pop at the re-hide.

findings.title: KO view in a corner puts the lens 0.13 m inside the building front, with the own shirt over 52-68% of the view for the whole KO; between two fighters it hovers 0.32 m over a dummy's head with the body clipped
findings.detail:
**How the lens gets its room.** _ko_room() casts one ray from the hips toward the pose on the chosen side, across the body. It shortens the reach to the hit minus ko_view_clearance_m, but then clamps it to ko_view_min_reach (0.4) (first_person_camera.gd:395). At reach 0.4 the lens sits 0.68 m out and 0.64 m up along the blocked line. When the wall is nearer than that, the lens ends up inside it.

**No fallback.** _choose_ko_side() only weighs the two across-the-body sides. In a corner, or lying diagonally against a wall, both sides are blocked. There is no other pose: along the body, higher and steeper, or overhead.

**Corner result.** The lens ends inside the building box, whose faces are back-face culled. The view becomes a dark, shadowed close-up of the player's own blue shirt and gray trousers for the whole 2.5 s. The body is never shown lying whole, which is what Game-boy approved.

**Flanked result.** Same root: the ray stops at Dummy2's capsule, so the lens hangs low right above that dummy's head (drawn as a dark blob at the bottom of the view). The player's body crosses the view and is clipped at the right edge.

**Untested.** test_ko_view covers a building front at one side, not a corner or a fighter on each side.
findings.repro:
godot --path . --write-movie captures/review_r3look/ko.avi --fixed-fps 60 --resolution 1280x720 res://captures/review_r3look/r3_probe.tscn -- "--act=KO7|KO9".

KO7: player at (19.3,0,-6.3) facing out of the corner, 3 HP, a sparring jab from 0.95 m knocks him back into the corner.

KO9: dummies at (1.3,0,0.4) and (-1.3,0,-0.4) in the player's frame, one jabbing from ahead.
findings.suggested_fix:
1. Never place the lens beyond the ray's hit: if the clamped reach would pass the hit, don't keep the line.
2. Try fallbacks in turn, scoring each by room and crowding like the two sides:
   - along the body (beyond the feet, then beyond the head);
   - straight up over the hips at a steeper pitch.
3. Check the final lens with a sphere query of ko_view_clearance_m against the world and enemy bodies, not just the one ray.
4. Add a corner case and a fighters-on-both-sides case to test_ko_view.gd: whole body in frame, lens outside all geometry, nothing within 0.25 m, own body at most a third.

findings.title: Hook stagger: the re-posed far fist now swings at the attacker's lens, 0.200 m on open floor and 0.145 m against a building front (gap-01's corner case still open)
findings.detail:
gap-04's re-pose folds the far (left) arm near the guard. When the stagger flings it, that fist is now the dummy's nearest part to the player's lens, and it comes inside 0.25 m even on open floor.

**Against the world.** With the dummy against the building front (the step-in against a pinned body, part of gap-01's evidence), it comes to 0.145 m over 58% of the view. The gap reviewer measured that case at 0.22 m and 47-50% at 8f5519f, before the re-pose. In the end-wall corner it is 0.166 m and 55%, against 0.14 m and 61% on the launch fixer's branch.

**Why the tests miss it.** tests/test_stagger_pose.gd measures the fist against the trunk axis, not the lens. The launch fixer left the corner hook to another package.

The far arm staying bent near the guard is approved. The defect is only where the fling points, toward the attacker's lens, and the lens rule it breaks.
findings.repro:
godot --path . --write-movie captures/review_r3look/hook.avi --fixed-fps 60 --resolution 1280x720 res://captures/review_r3look/r3_probe.tscn -- "--act=W7 |R01".

That is ragdoll_bot's 'Ragdoll: hook stagger' (P P P on a dummy 1.6 m ahead), and the same against the building front at z -6.55.
findings.suggested_fix:
1. Aim the folded far arm's fling up and away from the attacker in stagger_right_a/b and stagger_left. For example, the forearm rises beside the dummy's own head, not forward. That keeps the approved 'bent near the guard'.
2. Extend test_stagger_pose.gd, or a test_ragdoll lens test, to judge the hook through the attacker's real lens: nothing within 0.25 m, at most half the view, on open floor and with the dummy pinned.
3. For the pinned case, stop the magnetism step-in earlier when the target is against LAYER_WORLD (player.gd), as the launch fixer suggested.

findings.suggested_fix:
1. Change the tie-break among equally far spots so the dummy stands off-centre but in view, for example the spot nearest 45-60 degrees off the player's facing. Or score in-front spots by a minimum flat distance from the player, such as the sparring distance.
2. Or raise dummy_respawn_gap_m's default, so ring 1 sits about 1.2 m out.
3. Extend test_ko_blink's comeback test with a first-person share check: at most half the view.

findings.title: hit-04 is incomplete for the first-person haymaker: its delayed flash changes only 0.06-0.2% of the screen, against 2.2-9.4% for the other five first-person finishers
findings.detail:
With a seeded effects RNG, flash on against flash off, the delayed flash shows on exactly the 2 frames after the ink frame for the shove, backfist, stomp kick, push kick and pipe smash.

The first-person haymaker is the exception, so the hit-04 promise ('every finisher shows its flash') does not hold for it in the view Game-boy plays:
- At contact the step-in leaves the struck head above the top edge of the view.
- The large finisher burst and its word sit over the contact point and cover what is left.
- Its 2 flash frames change almost nothing.

The side-view haymaker's flash is hidden too (hit-05's area, dropped).
findings.repro: godot --path . --write-movie captures/review_r3look/fin_s.avi --fixed-fps 60 --resolution 1280x720 res://captures/review_r3look/fin_probe.tscn -- "--act=Hold P, release: haymaker", then the same with --tune=hit_flash_strength=0, and diff per frame (blend=difference).
findings.suggested_fix:
This is for Game-boy, with the open flash-size question (grab-05, hit-01). Options:
- in first person, when the contact is outside the view, flash the struck body's nearest visible part (for example the chest);
- offset the finisher burst from the contact so the flash core stays visible.

Also add the haymaker to test_hit_flash's per-frame finisher check through the real first-person view.
